findings: The standalone daemon's 1 ms accept loop is the largest idle wakeup source and drives roughly 867 voluntary context switches per second.
An attached client incidentally slows the daemon through its 50 ms socket read timeout, but combined daemon/client overhead still exceeds the release target.
The client performs a 10 Hz full redraw, global animation mutation, empty coordinator polling, and timed IPC receive even when nothing visible changes.
Host telemetry is collected at 1 Hz regardless of screen visibility and daemon telemetry is published at 1 Hz even with no clients.
Idle PTY and inactive BitBake tasks are event-driven; their action-bound deadlines are not steady-state wakeup sources.
There is no production heartbeat timer despite Ping/Pong wire support; connection liveness and saturation tolerance require separate correctness work.
